intro.author: 'The Preacher' (Hebrew Qoheleth), 'the son of David, king in Jerusalem' (1:1). Traditionally Solomon; many scholars think a later sage wrote in Solomon's voice, since the book never names him.
intro.written: Traditionally late in Solomon's reign (10th century BC). Many scholars date it between the 5th and 3rd centuries BC because of its late Hebrew style.
intro.audience: Israelites, especially the young (11:9; 12:1), wrestling with life's shortness, unfairness and unanswered questions
intro.setting: The Preacher speaks as a king who had every advantage (wisdom, wealth, pleasure and power) and tested whether any of it gave lasting gain. His key word, hebel (KJV 'vanity'), literally means breath or vapor: something real but fleeting and impossible to grasp. Jewish communities traditionally read the book at the Feast of Tabernacles.
intro.purpose: To strip away false hopes in work, wealth, pleasure and even wisdom, and to point readers to fearing God and receiving everyday life as His gift.
intro.bigIdea: Life 'under the sun' is fleeting and puzzling, so fear God and enjoy each day as His gift.

outline.title: Death, chance and the worth of wisdom
Live boldly and remember your Creator
